nodes.recap: chapter header + waking in the mud, burning tree, hospital
nodes.text:
-------------------------------
|          CHAPTER 24          |
-------------------------------


$CYour head is splitting.##

Hundreds of lights dance behind your eyes and a strong pins-and-needles
pervades everything.# You are shaking, in the dark.#
Before you are even fully conscious, before the pain makes sense,
your first thought is of Saberinne.##

You feel mutilated.# Your mind has closed back in on itself,
alone, without the sustaining presence of hers,
without any awareness beyond your own body.#
It is worse than going suddenly blind and deaf at once.##

You groan at the mental pain, which is louder than the physical.#
You roll on the ground, losing consciousness in short intervals.#
Then the smell of smoke cuts through everything
and brings you back: a tree a few meters away is on fire.#
You drag yourself clear, coughing, crawling through the mud
under relentless rain, until the darkness takes you again.##

$W----$C##

The ceiling is white.# A different white from Saberinne's hall,
hospital white, fluorescent, uniform, smelling of disinfectant
with a monitor beeping at measured, reassuring intervals.##

$G"Oh my God, Kriss, how are you?"$C Your mother
is looking at you, terrified, from beside the bed.##

You would like to say: very badly, worse than I look,
that you would have preferred not to wake up.#
But you will not frighten her more than she already is.##

$c"Fine... I think."$C##

She holds you for a long time.# $G"You were struck by lightning!
Do you realize?"$C##

You look at her without expression.#
After what you have been through,
it does not seem like a very unlikely event.##

nodes.recap: home - the silence inside him - the failed telepathic call
nodes.text:
They discharge you the next day.# Coming home, you say nothing.
You watch your world move past the window in the rain
and you think of Noi-Hert.# You cannot believe it was imagination.
You walked on that earth, breathed that air, ate food
that gave you strength.# And Saberinne...##

A knot in your throat stops every other thought.
You turn to the window to hide your eyes.##

Your house is exactly as you left it.# Six hours,
and everything is exactly as it was.##

You go to your room and sit on your bed
and wait to feel something,
and what you feel is silence.##

Where for most of a year there had been always something:
the sense of other minds nearby, the golden warmth
of Smiurl close by, Efeliah's chorus floating
right at the edge of perception, there is nothing now.#
Quiet, ordinary, absolute.##

$c<<So this is what it was like before.#
I had forgotten.# How did I live
for sixteen years in this silence
without even knowing it was silence?>>$C##

$CYou lie down and think: $Wthey are there.
Right now, they are there.#
Corolla is probably sharpening something.
Theo is probably sitting near a fire, looking at the dark.$C##

You think this until you fall asleep.# And you dream of Saberinne:
beautiful, near to you, speaking with that voice
that moves every atom in your body.##

You wake in the dead of night with tears on your face.#
You go to the window, wrap yourself in a blanket,
and look at the sleeping city.# The sky has cleared.#
You can see stars, constellations, the same ones you named
differently from the dark of the Great Desert.##

You send your thought outward, the way you could only do
on Noi-Hert, with a tremendous, lonely melancholy,
toward those depths, knowing that somewhere out there
that same planet is turning silently around its star,
without any trace of intelligent life that you can reach.##

Nothing answers.# Your mind has gone mute again.##

Frustrated, the sadness pressing on your chest like a stone,
you go back to sleep.##

nodes.recap: returning to school - everything feels diminished
nodes.text:
$c"Are you sure you want to go back to school?"$C your mother asks
over dinner the following evening.##

$c"Yes. I couldn't manage another day inside this house."$C##

Your father: $G"But you haven't recovered yet,
you should rest, stay in bed."$C
He doesn't know how true that is.##

$c"No. I've decided. I need to get back to my normal life..."$C##

They look at you without understanding.#
You stand, and say, $c"Trust me. It's better this way,"$C
and go to your room.# You have to come back, also in your mind,
to your world, your life.# You cannot go on living in Saberinne
while your body is here.# You would not survive it.# You might go mad.##

After more than an hour you manage to fall asleep.##

$W----$C##

School is not worse than you expected.# It is exactly as bad.##

The hallways are the same hallways, the faces the same faces,
and the particular smell of the cafeteria at 12:15
is precisely what it was, a combination of synthetic chicken
and something that is probably not actually a cleaning product.##

You sit in your classes and take notes and are polite
and eat lunch and do homework and none of it is $Wwrong$C exactly.##

But the scrubland south of Ayonn you remember in colors
that have no names on Earth, and the first sight of the sea,
and Smiurl flying across a canyon on a rope
complaining every centimeter of the way,
and Corolla teaching you to cheat at cards
and daring you to say something about it.##

You carry this like a stone in your chest,
not heavy exactly, a weight that is also ballast,
something that keeps you in the water
instead of drifting away entirely.##

Months pass.##

You pass the tree on the way to school every morning.#
The rain put out the fire.# Several branches are bare and scorched,
the bark blackened on one side.#
Even that tree carries the mark of what happened.##

It is a Tuesday in winter.##

The kind of Tuesday that is identical to all the other Tuesdays
except that when you arrive early and sit at your usual seat
your classmate from the row behind leans forward
and whispers: $W"Hey, Kriss, there's a new student today"$C
and nods toward the door.##

$c<<A new student.# Fine.#
I was a new student once,
on an entirely different planet.>>$C##

$CThe teacher comes in.##

$W"Please sit, Sabrina. Class, say hello!"$C##

You are looking at your notebook.##

She moves between the desks and your classmates laugh
and make the noise classmates make, and you keep your eyes down,
and then she stops and asks, of the empty desk
that has been empty beside you for as long as you can remember:#

$WSabrina:$C $W"Excuse me, is anyone sitting here?"$C##

You look up.##

nodes.recap: the eyes - the recognition - the ending
nodes.text:
Her eyes are green.##

Exactly that particular green, the specific green
of deep water when the sun is at exactly the right angle,
the only green that exists in exactly one way on two worlds.##

Time stops.# The same way it stopped in the elliptical hall.##

You are gripping the edge of your desk
because you need something to hold onto,
and you are breathing with some difficulty,
and for one suspended instant of silence
the classroom around you does not exist.##

You say: $c"$G$WSaberinne$G$c!"$C##

She looks at you, surprised, with an expression you know.#
You would know it in the dark, you would know it at the end of the world.
She is not expecting a welcome quite like this one.##

$G"You must have misheard..."$C she says,
smiling despite herself. $G"...my name is Sabrina."$C##

You cannot stop staring.# She holds your gaze,
amused, steady, with those eyes.#
The teacher says something about sitting down.# She sits.##

She arranges her things, opens her notebook,
and after a moment she turns and looks at you,
in that way that makes your heart tear itself in half,
and says:#

$G"You know, Kriss...#
I have the impression I've seen you somewhere before."$C##
